correctness.rationale: The finite killed generator uniquely determines all mean times. Averaging and differencing the two gate-conditioned backward equations yields a quadratic discrete Poisson profile and a hyperbolic screened-discrete-harmonic profile. A reflecting endpoint fixes the unique constant, proving the exact all-size formula including \(N=1\); differentiation and scaling give the monotonicity and diffusive crossover. Independent rational full-generator elimination matches 520 exact cases (\(1\le N\le 13\)); 9 scaling diagnostics and 24 monotonicity checks support, but do not prove, the quantified algebra.

originality.rationale: The closest primary 2011 article has antiphase switching gates in a smooth planar narrow-escape problem but only small-gate asymptotic results, not an all-N discrete path solution. The 2016 tree/interval paper studies a pair of endpoints that are both absorbing or both reflecting in the same environment state, not complementary endpoints; the 2016 switched-PDE framework establishes equations, not this closed finite-lattice profile. The original claimed additions are the global location-independent delay, rational Chebyshev recurrence, and exact diffusive-rate crossover, not the general backward-equation method or qualitative faster switching. Targeted indexed mathematical-results collection queries and primary text checks found no covering result; residual risks are explicit.

value.rationale: A physically motivated exact finite-size model of complementary escape gates has an all-site closed mean-time profile with a gate-dependent correction independent of source location; the \(N^{-2}\) diffusion-scale transition and its exact scaling function are quantified, not inferred from finite enumeration. Such a closed benchmark distinguishes antiphase from synchronous gates in kinetic and first-passage modeling and is an all-parameter structural classification rather than a tiny numerical gain.
